API reference¶

Web application and routes¶

Flask factory, injectable ETL dependencies, and observable busy-state policy.

class src.flask_app.ServiceState(scraper: ~typing.Callable, cleaner: ~typing.Callable, loader: ~typing.Callable, query: ~typing.Callable, lock: object = <factory>, analysis: dict | None = None)[source]¶

Dependencies and cache owned by one app, never shared between factories.

src.flask_app.index()[source]¶

GET / or /analysis: render the cached snapshot, initializing it once.

src.flask_app.pull_data()[source]¶

POST /pull-data: scrape, clean, and load; return 409 when busy.

src.flask_app.update_analysis()[source]¶

POST /update-analysis: refresh the snapshot or return 409 while busy.

src.flask_app.create_app(test_config=None, *, engine=None, scraper=None, cleaner=None, loader=None, query=None)[source]¶

Create an app with optional configuration and dependency overrides.

DATABASE_URL comes from configuration or the environment. Injected loader and query functions allow web tests without opening a database. Production and database-test requests execute the same ETL code.

Backward-compatible factory import: flask --app src.app:create_app.

Scraping¶

Bounded survey scraping with injectable HTTP transport and pure parsing.

src.scrape._build_urls(pages)[source]¶

Return the first 1-10 survey page URLs; avoid an unbounded pull.

src.scrape._parse_html(html_text)[source]¶

Parse supplied five-column survey HTML and optional detail rows.

Header/detail rows are ignored. Details cannot leak from the next result. Missing identity fields are reported by the cleaner before persistence.

src.scrape.scrape_data(pages=1, *, http_get=None)[source]¶

Fetch bounded pages with TLS verification and a 15 s timeout.

Pass an HTTP double in tests. HTTP failures propagate before any database write so the web layer can report failure without committing a partial batch.

src.scrape.save_data(data, filename)[source]¶

Save raw scraper records as UTF-8 JSON (legacy helper).

src.scrape.load_data(filename)[source]¶

Read a previously saved raw scraper JSON file (legacy helper).

Cleaning¶

Normalize original scraped/enriched records without requiring a live LLM.

src.clean.parse_str(value)[source]¶

Strip scalar text; missing, structured, and textual nulls become None.

src.clean.parse_float(value)[source]¶

Read a finite number, also accepting legacy values such as ‘GPA 3.8’.

src.clean.parse_date(value)[source]¶

Accept Python dates and the original ISO/abbreviated/full month formats.

src.clean.canonical_url(value)[source]¶

Normalize a stable result URL while retaining ID-bearing query strings.

src.clean.clean_record(record)[source]¶

Map legacy keys to Module 3 columns and validate required fields.

Existing LLM-generated fields are retained; missing enrichment stays NULL. IDs are allocated by PostgreSQL. Source URLs deduplicate repeated pulls.

src.clean.clean_data(records, *, enrich=None)[source]¶

Validate records; optionally call an injected enrichment adapter.

The adapter takes and returns a dictionary. The default path needs no model download or external LLM service; tests can supply a deterministic double.

Loading and import¶

Transactional and idempotent inserts into the original applicant table.

src.load_data.read_records(filename)[source]¶

Read a JSON array or newline-delimited JSON exported by Module 2/3.

src.load_data.load_data(records, engine)[source]¶

Insert a batch atomically; return the count of new source URLs.

PostgreSQL enforces URL uniqueness even with concurrent writers. Any failed insert rolls back the entire batch; duplicates leave the existing row intact. Records must already be normalized by src.clean.clean_data().

Schema and configuration¶

The Module 3 applicant schema, with explicit connection configuration.

class src.models.Applicant(**kwargs)[source]¶

One survey submission; its canonical URL is the uniqueness key.

All sixteen Module 3 column names and their types are preserved. Unknown optional values remain NULL; core identity fields must be present.

src.models.make_engine(database_url=None)[source]¶

Build a lazy PostgreSQL engine from an argument or DATABASE_URL.

src.models.init_db(engine)[source]¶

Create missing tables; never drop or truncate existing application data.

Analysis queries¶

Module 3’s eleven analysis questions, computed in PostgreSQL.

src.query_data.empty_analysis()[source]¶

Return the complete template contract for an empty applicant table.

src.query_data.fetch_applicants(engine)[source]¶

Return all sixteen Module 3 fields as dictionaries ordered by p_id.

src.query_data.get_analysis_data(engine)[source]¶

Return numeric q1-q11/diff results; formatting belongs to the template.

Q2 excludes unknown citizenship. Q5 includes all Fall 2025 decisions; Q11 includes international Spring 2027 decisions. Empty rates are 0.0; missing averages are None. A repeatable-read snapshot keeps all answers consistent.

Compatibility entry point for the original ORM analysis module.

src.orm_queries.run_queries(engine)[source]¶

Compute all eleven questions using the shared SQLAlchemy query layer.
